title: Simple Countdown Timer Webpage
problem_statement: Users need a simple, distraction-free countdown timer that works instantly in a web browser — no installation, no login, no setup. Common use cases include time-boxing tasks, managing presentations, timing workouts, cooking, or any activity where a quick visual countdown helps maintain focus and urgency.
target_users: Presenters and public speakers (timing talks and presentations)

functional_requirements.description: Display the remaining countdown time in large, clearly readable format (HH:MM:SS or MM:SS depending on duration).
acceptance_criteria: Time is displayed in the center of the page with large font size (minimum 72px on desktop).
Format auto-adapts: durations under 1 hour show MM:SS; durations >= 1 hour show HH:MM:SS.
Leading zeros are always shown (e.g., 05:03, not 5:3).
The display updates every second.

functional_requirements.description: Allow the user to set a custom countdown duration via manual input.
acceptance_criteria: User can enter hours, minutes, and seconds via separate input fields or a combined time picker.
Input fields default to 00:05:00 (5 minutes).
Invalid inputs (negative values, non-numeric) are rejected with inline validation feedback.
Maximum settable duration is 99:59:59.

functional_requirements.description: Provide quick-select preset buttons for common durations.
acceptance_criteria: Preset buttons exist for: 1 min, 3 min, 5 min, 10 min, 15 min, 30 min, 60 min.
Clicking a preset immediately updates the timer display to that duration.
If a timer is running, clicking a preset resets and sets the new duration (timer stops).

functional_requirements.description: Provide Start, Pause, and Reset buttons to control the countdown.
acceptance_criteria: Start button begins the countdown from the currently set time.
Pause button halts the countdown while preserving remaining time; button label changes to 'Resume' while paused.
Reset button stops the countdown and restores the display to the originally set time.
Start button is disabled (or changes to Pause) while counting down.
Pause/Resume button is disabled when the timer is not running.
Reset button is always enabled when the display differs from the originally set time.

functional_requirements.description: Alert the user when the countdown reaches zero via visual change and an optional audio notification.
acceptance_criteria: When timer reaches 00:00, the display flashes or changes color (e.g., red background pulse).
A browser notification API alert is triggered (with user permission).
An audio beep or alarm sound plays (at least 3 beeps or 3 seconds of sound).
The page title updates to 'TIME'S UP!' or similar indicator so users on other tabs can see it.

functional_requirements.description: Ensure the countdown remains accurate even when the browser tab is in the background.
acceptance_criteria: Timer calculates remaining time based on the difference between current wall-clock time and the target end time (Date-based), rather than relying on setInterval tick count.
When user returns to a backgrounded tab, the displayed time is correct (within 1 second of actual elapsed time).
Timer drift over 10 minutes is no more than 1 second.

functional_requirements.description: Support responsive design so the timer is usable on both desktop and mobile browsers.
acceptance_criteria: Layout is single-column and stacks vertically on screens narrower than 480px.
All buttons and inputs have touch-friendly tap targets (minimum 44x44px per WCAG).
Timer font size scales down appropriately on small screens (minimum 48px).
No horizontal scrolling required on any screen width >= 320px.

non_functional_requirements.description: Page must load and become interactive in under 2 seconds on a 3G connection.
Countdown accuracy must stay within 1 second of true elapsed time for durations up to 1 hour, regardless of tab focus.
No user data is collected or transmitted; the page must function without any network requests after initial load.
Interface must be intuitive enough that a first-time user can set and start a timer within 10 seconds without instructions.
This is a single-user client-side application. No server-side scaling concerns apply.

constraints: Must be implemented as a single self-contained HTML file (HTML + CSS + JS inline) with zero external dependencies, or minimally a small set of files in the same directory.
No backend server, database, or API calls required.
Must work in the latest 2 versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
Must not require any browser extensions or plugins.
Total page weight (HTML + CSS + JS + assets) must not exceed 200 KB.
assumptions: The timer is used for short to medium durations (seconds to a few hours), not multi-day countdowns.
No user accounts, login, or data persistence across sessions is needed.
A simple, clean visual design is acceptable — no specific brand or theme is required.
The audio alert will use the Web Audio API or an inline <audio> element with a generated/embedded sound rather than external audio files.
The countdown stops at 00:00 without automatically counting up (a 'stop at zero' behavior).
The browser Notification API may be used, but the timer should function fully even if the user denies notification permission.

clarifying_questions.question: Should the timer automatically start counting UP after reaching zero (a stopwatch-style overflow), stop at zero, or loop back to the original set time?
Do you want a dark mode / light mode toggle, or is a single default color scheme acceptable?
Should the timer state persist across page refreshes (using localStorage), or is it acceptable for a refresh to reset to defaults?
Do you prefer a fullscreen immersive design (like a dedicated timer app) or a standard webpage layout with the timer as the central element?
